Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City Council.
Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order and
decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of
the City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.

  •  The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park
  City Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each
  speaker will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed
  on the City Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the
  City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct
  disruptive to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of
  Procedure or conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council
  Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must
  be directed to the Mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required
for the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

PUBLIC COMMENT

For both open and closed session, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per
Huntington Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other
speakers and may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one
meeting to another. This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled
public hearing items.

All comments or queries shall be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown
Act, no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing
on the posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide
direction to staff, or schedule a matter for a future meeting.
ADDITIONS/DELETIONS TO AGENDA

Items of business may be added to the agenda upon a motion adopted by a minimum two-
thirds vote finding that there is a need to take immediate action and that the need for action
came to the attention of the City or Agency subsequent to the agenda being posted. Items
may be deleted from the agenda upon the request of staff or Council.

CITY MANAGER

  1. CONSIDERATION OF FILLING VACANT COUNCIL MEMBER POSITION

Per the Municipal Code from the day a vacancy is made on the City Council, the City Council
has 60 days to fill the vacancy.
The City Manager presented the alternatives that Councilmembers could take in regards to
filling vacant council member commissions.
1) By adopting Resolution No. 2025-06.
  1) FIlling Vacancy by Special Election to be held not less than 114 days from the call of
  the special election; or
  2) FIlling Vacancy by appointment until the next regularly scheduled election, scheduled
  to be held on March 3, 2026; or
  3) take necessary related actions that may be desirable.

On February 18, 2025; the position held by Councilmember Esmeralda Castillo was deemed
vacant following an investigation into a complaint received by the City of Huntington Park in
September of 2024. The complaint alleged Councilmember Castillo was not a resident in the
CIty. The investigation confirmed that she did not have residency in the CIty of Huntington Park.
As a result, City Council is obligated in filling the vacancy either by appointment or by special
election.

If the council calls for a special election, the City Council will have to establish a special election
date within 114 days from the call of the special election. The individual elected will hold the
office until the expiration of the term March of 2028. County clerk office has no election
scheduled from now until that date, thus this election can not be consolidated with any other
county, state, or election and would be determined a special election. The election would also
come at the City’s expense which could be upwards of 500,000 dollars. Staff will prepare
resolutions

Or appoint an individual to fill the vacancy until the next general election scheduled for March 3,
2026. City of Huntington Park Municipal Code does not hold a formal process on the
appointment process so council would need to create one. Councilmembers can solicit
applications, and conduct interviews prior to making an appointment. City Council may choose
but is not required to solicit and or conduct interviews prior to making the appointment. If council
chooses to make an appointment, it must be done within 60 days of the vacancy. Since vacancy
was made on February 18, 2025, council members would need to fill vacancy by April 21, 2025
(since April 18, 2025 falls on a Saturday). Appointees must be a resident in the City of
 Huntington Park, must be a registered voter, and must be the age of 18 years old at time of
appointment. If council serves as appointee he would be required to run in the 2026 general
election if interested in retaining his position. If elected in 2026, individuals would serve the
remainder of the term (expires in March 2028).

Investigation Detail Breifing: Council and the Public were briefed with basics regarding the
investigation into Councilmember Castillo’s residency. As it is an active investigation only brief
information was provided. Once completed more information would be granted.

MOTION: Councilmember Sanabria motioned to appoint adopted RESOLUTION 2025-06 and
fill the vacancy by appointment. With a deadline application on Friday, March 28, 2025. Public
candidacy three-minute presentations will be conducted at the regularly scheduled city council
meeting of Monday, April 7, 2025; and, possible appointments being on Monday, April 7, 2025
and/ or guaranteed appointment at a following special or regularly scheduled City Council
Meeting on or before April 21, 2025 (the 60 day deadline) of the individuals who applied and
presented. The motion was then second by Vice Mayor Flores. The motion passed by majority
consent.

AYES: Council Member (s): Martinez, Sanabria, and Vice Mayor Flores

NOES: Council Member (s): Mayor Macias. (Mayor Macias wanted to state that the process is
illegal).

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Sanabria: Thanks to all staff and community members who came out tonight. Decision to
uphold Municipal Code was why they were elected. Since last time there was a change on
council about ten years ago. Was part of that group who tried to make changes for the
community. He failed to see Rent Stabalization, changing Huntington Park’s status to a
sanctuary city. All we saw was a change in vendors. But the material lives of residents did not
change. He mentioned the aquatics center. He pushed for the palestinian ordinance and the
lobbying ordinance.
 Martinez: Thank you to all the community members who came out. All facts will come out.
Time will rebuild everything, and we’ll have a better understanding of how the city operates and
how they make decisions and how they move forward.

Flores: Thank you Staff.

Macias: Thanks Staff and Directors. Very proud of the work that has been done in the last 12
years. There’s more work to do. Pool project was stalled due to the county measures, and
covid. Resources had to be redistributed from pool projects to keeping individuals alive.
Distributing food distribution, mask distribution, senior income for a year, income for struggling
folks, etc. Getting transportation money for public transit, and street improvement. That work
has been done in the last 10 years, and there’s more work to do. It’s unfortunate what happened
here to Councilmember Castillo, actions were taken that were illegal. She nor any other
members of the council were judges to make this kind of decision of who and who does not live
in the city. She always carries a little constitution book in her purse, and tonight Councilmember
Castillo’s constitutional rights were violated. People have died to fight for these constitutional
rights. That action was wrong and should’ve never been done. There’s always been
disagreements but not to this magnitude. That’s why I voted No. The City was placed on Notice
by an attorney and we should all be worried.

  attorney-client privilege to facilitate cooperation with investigative authorities;

  *Prior to this motion. Councilmember Martinez and City Manager Ricardo Reyes
  escorted themselves out of the council chambers.

  Motion: Councilmember Sanabria motioned to waiver the conflict allowing Attorney
  Andrew Sarega to represent City Manager Ricardo Reyes and Council Member
  Eduardo “Eddie” Martinez in matters related to the investigation. Attorney Sarega
  clearly stated in his statement that the City Attorney and Councilmember will be
  personally responsible for paying all costs associated with this case and their
  representation. Additionally, if any conflicts of interest are to arise in the future, then
  he will abstain from representing Councilmember Martinez and City Manager Reyes
  any further. Mayor Macias stated she was not comfortable with voting on this agenda
  item. Mayor Macias then proceeded to step off the Dias, opting not to vote. Vice
  Mayor Flores motioned to take over as chair. [At this point a member of the Public
  {Linda Caballeros}, stepped up and stated out loud that the Chambers do not have
  a Quorum, requesting the City Clerk clarify ‘it’]. Following this incident, Mayor Macias
  returned to the Dias. Vice Mayor Flores seconded the motion with the request that
  when not if a conflict of interest arises, then Mr. Sarega relinquishes all legal
  representation of Councilmember Eduardo ‘Eddie’ Martinez, and City Manager
  Ricardo Reyes. Motion carried by majority consent.

City Attorney: Dear Mayor and Members of the City Council, after doing careful
consideration this letter will serve to inform the city council of the city of Huntington Park
that I individually and my law Firm Alvarez, Glassman and Colvin will be exercising our
rights to terminate our services pursuing section 12 of the agreement for City Attorney
Services dated April 6 2015 which reads in part the firm may terminated its services at
any time with the city for good cause, good cause exists if the city refuses to cooperate
with firm refuses to follow firms advice on material matters or otherwise made its
representation unreasonably difficult. Over the recent months the circumstances
surrounding activities and action taken meets the definition of good cause is stand above.
The current environment and lack of communication with my office has made our
continued representation unreasonably difficult to continue to serve as City Attorney. Out
of respect and obligation to the attorney-client privilege I will not articulate the facts or
circumstances that led to this decision. Alvares, Glassman and Colvin is proud of the
excellent legal services that our firm has provided to the City for nearly a decade. I and
my law firm will continue to provide legal services for the next 30 days or until a new city
attorney or law firm is selected to take the position as your legal counsel. I thank you for
the opportunity to serve as your city attorney. Very Truly yours Arnold M. Glasssman
managing partner at Alvarez, Glassman, and Colvin.

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS
Councilmember Sanabria: Thank you staff during the tumultuous time. In 2013, he was
in the place of the public. He supported the change and wanted to see it be implemented
in the city. He wanted to see real change in the city. We have only established a bare
minimum base, which is good but not enough. We’ve only seen a change in vendors and
not the quality of life of our constituents. He wanted to see rent control pass, which we
saw and although it is not perfect it is a large step in the right direction. We also passed
the lobbying ordinance. When he arrived, we saw a lot of these issues happening in our
community. He is happy that this ordinance is bringing a lot of these issues to life. This
ordinance is holding people accountable. He is in support of introducing term limits. We
need to protect our infrastructure including our water systems. He doesn’t want to see
the water rights sold. We as councilmembers need to protect our water system and
ensure rates don’t skyrocket the community. This is a sanctuary city and wants to get the
message out to the community. He finds it interesting how they [Councilmember
Sanabria, Martinez, Vice Mayor Flores, and City Manager Ricardo Reyes] were served
with a lawsuit; however, other people who have been written about taking money from
vendors and has served for twelve years has not been served. He is disappointed with
the aquatics center. During high school, he used to skate at the skate park in Salt Lake
Park until 9pm sometimes. When the skate park was taken away, he got upset; however,
he is hurt that the lot where the skate park used to be is still an empty lot. He has to take
son out to parks in other communities because we don’t have parks in this community.
He would like for us to better understand the performance evaluation on some of the
contracts that the city has been a part of. Especially those who appear on the Form
700s. He wants to let the public know that there are folks on the council who do stand
with them. He would also like to know more about the CAL700 forms, and why is it that
the City Attorney and other councilmembers appeared on this ‘one’ person’s form.

Councilmember Martinez: Thank you to residents who came out. He didn’t say much
today because he was here to listen. His home was served with a search warrant, scary
times especially for elderly mother. He is cooperating with DA office in the investigation.
Yesterday, 2/27/2025 he had a 3 hour testimony. City should be giving any and all
documents with the DA’s office for cooperation. He is okay with term limits [2 terms]. We
should begin to investigate the term limits, because essentially once an individual is in
 office they just get rolled over to the next election until they retire. He doesn’t agree with
this. We should also begin to assess the PACs.

Vice Mayor Flores: Thank you to the residents and community. He wants the
community to imagine getting paid 120,000 dollars for a few hours of work. A few months
ago that is what he discovered when he was looking at payments that were going out
regarding the pool project. Upward Solution was doing outreach work for the pool
project. Robert Urteaga who is the owner of Upward Solution is leading his recall efforts,
and his understanding that the financier is Effren Martinez. Luis Vecerra [Graciela Ortiz’s
nephew] was the individual who served him with the recall. The last council meeting
there were several processors chasing him to serve him with the recall. There were
individuals who were reporting his location and every move. His recall response: He is a
marine and has served in war twice. He isn’t scared to go to war with his community.
Vice Mayor Flores’s official statement: I, Vice Mayor, Arturo Flores, categorically
reject the misleading and defamatory allegations contained in this notice. This effort
does not reflect my record of service but appears to be a politically motivated attempt to
hinder transparency and accountability. This recall follows my commitment to
investigating the Failed Pool Project, which has cost taxpayers approximately $12 million
over five years with nothing to show but an empty lot. I believe this recall is a retaliatory
effort by those seeking to avoid accountability for mismanagement. Facts: Residency: I
have lived in our city throughout my tenure on the Council; Investigations: No active
investigation against me by the city; Confidential Plates: legally obtained and used for
security purposes to protect myself and my family for any potential retaliation;
Compensation: Salary adjustment for council members was implemented under
California Senate Bill 329, after 17 years; False Allegations: The claim against me
regarding misconduct are entirely false and baseless. Instead of wasting at least
$500,000 taxpayer dollars on an unfounded recall. Let’s focus on: Investigating the
Failed Pool Project; Tracing millions of unaccounted dollars; Restoring faith and trust in
our local government.

Mayor Macias: Thanked all residents who came to public comment. She’s confident in
the process of the investigation. Thanked DA police for being cordial in the process of
when he went to her home. Pretty confident in process of investigation. Thanks to
employees and directors. We have very hard working employees. Assure them that as
we continue process of investigation, that they are appreciated and cared for and that in
the process of all of this it is easy to forget the humanity of employees, and directors that
are just trying to provide a service to the community. Including Police Department, Parks
and Recreation, Public Works, and staff here tonight. She feels confident where she
stands as a councilmember, resident, and woman on where she stands. She grew up
and lives in the city. She’s a caregiver. She is confident in the process, that an aquatics
center is not an illusion for the community and can be a reality in the near future.

Respectfully submitted

Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk
